. [In mythology, the sun is regarded as a son of Kaśyapa and
 Aditi. He is represented as moving in a chariot drawn by seven horses,
 with Aruṇa for his charioteer. He is also represented as all-seeing, the
 constant beholder of the good and bad deeds of mortals. Samjñā (or Chāyā
 or Aśvinī) was his principal wife, by whom he had Yama and Yamunā,
 the two Aśvins and Saturn. He is also described as having been the father
 of Manu Vaivasvata, the founder of the solar race of kings.]
